Score: 91, set by the Rater. Well inside A on every reading, led by earnings and buybacks rather than the multiple, and the three-year check (+86% to +120%) confirms it. Placed at the lower end of A's top half, below the 95 that 60%+ maps to, for the fat lower tail: the trough of -12% to -29% on 6.5-7.0x EBITDA, a downward-skewed EPS cone and frontier repatriation and currency tails.

13Summary conclusion

The decisionBuy a high-quality, contracted lease-up compounder at a frontier discount, expecting about +65 percent to December 2027 at a fair 20x multiple and about +39 percent even if the multiple does not move, while holding through an unfavourable run of news in November 2026 and March 2027.

The operating case is about as predictable as any in European infrastructure; the equity case is a leveraged residual on a frontier sovereign layer. The demand surge of 2026 is real, broad and partly front-loaded. It has already been converted into contracted revenue that lifts FY2027 EBITDA by about 12.6 percent whatever operators do next, and the company's habit of guiding below its run-rate means operating guidance and estimates will keep rising through 2027. The internal change is a cash-funded pivot to distributions, led by a management with an outstanding delivery record and a few governance wobbles in 2026. The leverage structure turns high-single-digit EBITDA growth into 20 to 100 percent EPS growth, and the same structure leaves the EPS line hostage to currency, tax and finance items that the company neither guides nor controls.

The investment question is therefore one of sequencing and of the multiple. The unfavourable surprises arrive first: a sequential fall in additions on 5 November, a FY2026 EPS print about a quarter below consensus in March 2027, and a visible deceleration of reported growth in H2 2027. The favourable surprises follow: FY2027 guidance at or above consensus, the buyback showing in the share count, early delivery and a refresh of the 2030 targets, a step-up in distributions as leverage falls through 3.0x, and the DRC renewals of 2028 to 2029, which I expect to be traded for term rather than cut.

The market values the stock at 8.5x EBITDA with a locked frontier discount, and the model's return rests on a P/E re-rating to 26.28x that I regard as a ceiling, not a central case. From earnings and buybacks alone, at an unchanged multiple, the shares return about +39 percent to December 2027 and about +86 percent to June 2029. At my fair multiple of about 20x, they return about +65 percent and +120 percent. The trough is 145p to 180p.

The skew is positive at the EBITDA and cash level, and symmetric to negative at the EPS level. The probability of upgrades to operating guidance and EBITDA estimates is unusually high, and the probability of EPS upgrades in the next six months is low. This is a Demand-driven EPSU setup with a mechanical deleveraging kicker, bought while the market is focused on the noisy earnings line rather than the contracted cash line.

76

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength: 75, set by the Rater. Strong, funded and partly contracted external demand (72) and a narrow but well-executed capital-allocation pivot (64) are already turning into forecast profits through a highly geared model: FY2027 EBITDA is about 12.6% higher largely on carry already contracted, and EPS doubles then compounds about 26% a year (top-fifth consensus growth). It sits below Richard's Arteche 80 because part of the demand is borrowed from 2027-28 and the profit change reaches EPS through noisy, unguided lines below EBITDA.

70

Foundations' Robustness: 73, set by the Rater. A concentrated, contract-protected tower position with operating lines among the most stable and predictable in the Universe (ten years of EBITDA growth through Ghana's default, 1% churn cap, indexed non-cancellable leases) and a management whose operating delivery is outstanding (80) make a robust base, which per Richard's CVS example counts for more than the ordinary reported returns. It is held below the 75-80 band's top by a defensive moat without pricing power, 72% customer concentration facing the DRC renewals, a frontier sovereign layer and 3.4-3.8x leverage.

68

Setups' Fit/Crispness: 78, set by the Rater. A clear Demand-driven EPSU in substance: a dated, multi-operator capex step-up feeding contracted tenancies onto a fixed site and finance base, with the capacity (build time 102 days, 99.99% uptime) and delivery record in place, plus a mechanical buyback and deleveraging kicker. One element is loose: the demand is partly front-loaded (additions already falling in 2027) and it reaches EPS, the setup's defining line, through unguided tax, finance and FX lines; the FY2026 EPS miss and what consensus holds are timing and are not counted here.

41

Case Riskiness: 45, set by the Rater. A simple, one-driver, contracted operating case is offset for the shares by the +/-30% downward-skewed EPS cone on unguided financial lines, frontier repatriation and currency tails, 72% customer concentration and dependence on the multiple, as in topic 9 (41). It sits a little above topic 9 because, unlike a stretched multiple, today's is mid-range in its own history and near cheap against peers, which limits the de-rating risk.

Appendix: a comment from the Financial Analyst on reporting basis

Our model keeps one reporting basis for history and forecasts. The checks below suggest that consensus may use a different basis for some lines, so part of the gap between our forecasts and consensus on those lines may not be a difference of view. Nothing has been adjusted in the model.

What the checks found:

  • Consensus net income for FY2026 is 99.55, +112.7% against 46.80 in FY2025 on our model's basis; consensus revenue moves +10.9%.

Facts in the data file that commonly explain such a gap:

  • Non-controlling (minority) interests on the balance sheet: 38.6, 1.3% of market capitalisation. Our model does not deduct them; consensus earnings per share do.
  • Amortisation of acquired intangibles over the last twelve months: -34.7 before tax (-0.03 per share); our model's FY2025 history does not exclude it (its EBITA equals EBIT). Brokers' adjusted figures often exclude it.
  • Hybrid bond coupons and capitalised leases are not in the data file; check the company's reporting where relevant.

How to read this page

Every rating of this stock on one page: the Rater's 1-100 number, its letter and the Rater's own reason (at most three sentences, taken from the ratings file; nothing newly written). The number is the company's approximate standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10; 50 = typical). A letter follows its item's rule: rank among the stocks scored (A the top 10%; B+ and B the next 15%; C+, C and C- the next 25%; D the next 25%; F the bottom 25%); or Richard's cut-offs on the measure for the four numerical topics (forecast financials, current momentum, the fair multiple, total shareholder return). On the change-forces items the number carries a sign (50 = neither positive nor negative) and the letter is the rank, so read the two together. "9th of 30 stocks scored" is the stock's place on that item. A dashed badge is provisional (fewer than 30 stocks scored).
